en svømmehal.explanation: "En svømmehal" means "an indoor swimming pool". It is built from "at svømme" (to swim) and "en hal" (a hall).

en svømmetur.explanation: "En svømmetur" means "a swim". It is built from "at svømme" (to swim) and "en tur" (a trip).

en sweater.explanation: "En sweater" means "a sweater". To say you are wearing one, use "at have ... på" (literally "to have ... on"): "Jeg har en sweater på" (I am wearing a sweater).

en sygdom.explanation: "En sygdom" means "a disease". It is built from "syg" (sick). To say a person is sick, use "syg" instead: "Hun er syg" (She is sick).

en sygemelding.explanation: "En sygemelding" means "a sick note / sick leave". To say you call in sick, use "at melde sig syg" (literally "to report oneself sick"): "Jeg melder mig syg i dag" (I am calling in sick today).

en sygeplejerske.explanation: "En sygeplejerske" means "a nurse". It is built from "sygepleje" (nursing). To talk about a male nurse, use the same word: "Min bror er sygeplejerske" (My brother is a nurse).

en synagoge.explanation: "En synagoge" means "a synagogue". English speakers should note the Danish spelling ends in "-goge", not "-gogue". A well-known synagogue in Denmark is in "Krystalgade" in Copenhagen.

en synd.explanation: "En synd" means "a sin". To say you feel sorry for someone, use "synd" with no religious meaning: "Det er synd for ham" (I feel sorry for him). To say something is a pity, use it the same way: "Det er synd, at det regner" (It is a pity that it rains).

en synder.explanation: "En synder" means "a sinner". To ask who is to blame for something small, use it for the culprit: "Hvem er synderen?" (Who is the culprit?)

en synkronisering.explanation: "En synkronisering" means "a sync". It comes from "at synkronisere" (to synchronize). To say sound and picture are not timed together, use it for the timing: "Synkroniseringen af lyd og billede er dårlig" (The sync of sound and picture is bad).

en synsvinkel.explanation: "En synsvinkel" means "a point of view / angle". It is built from "syn" (sight) and "en vinkel" (an angle). To talk about the real place you look from, use it for a physical angle: "Fra den synsvinkel kan man se hele byen" (From that angle you can see the whole city).

en syre.explanation: "En syre" means "an acid". It is close to "sur" (sour). To say something tastes sour, use "sur": "Æblet er surt" (The apple is sour).

en sæk.explanation: "En sæk" means "a sack". To name what is in the sack, put it after: "en sæk mel" (a sack of flour). To say backpack, add "ryg" (back) in front: "en rygsæk" (a backpack).

en sæl.explanation: "En sæl" means "a seal". To mean the seal on a document, use a different word, "et segl": "Brevet har et rødt segl" (The letter has a red seal).

en sælger.explanation: "En sælger" means "a salesperson". It comes from "at sælge" (to sell). To say what someone does for a living: "Hun er sælger i en bilforretning" (She is a salesperson at a car dealership).

en sælgerske.explanation: "En sælgerske" means "a saleswoman". It is "en sælger" (a salesperson) with the ending "-ske", which makes the word feminine. The same ending is in "en sygeplejerske" (a nurse).

en sæson.explanation: "En sæson" means "a season", as in a TV season or a sports season. To name the time when something is in demand, put the thing before it: "jordbærsæsonen" (the strawberry season). For spring, summer, fall and winter, use "en årstid" (a season of the year): "Min yndlingsårstid er sommer" (My favorite season is summer).

en sæsonbillet.explanation: "En sæsonbillet" means "a season ticket". It is built from "en sæson" (a season) and "en billet" (a ticket). A similar word is "et sæsonkort" (a season pass): "Jeg har købt et sæsonkort" (I have bought a season pass).

en sætning.explanation: "En sætning" means "a sentence", as in grammar. To ask someone to write one: "Skriv en sætning" (Write a sentence). For a prison sentence, use "en dom" (a verdict): "Han fik en dom på to år" (He got a sentence of two years).

en sø.explanation: "En sø" means "a lake". Do not mix it up with "et hav" (a sea): "Skibet sejler på havet" (The ship sails on the sea).

en søgemaskine.explanation: "En søgemaskine" means "a search engine". It is built from "at søge" (to search) and "en maskine" (a machine). To say you search online: "Jeg søger på nettet efter en cykel" (I am searching online for a bike).

en sølvfisk.explanation: "En sølvfisk" means "a silverfish". It is built from "sølv" (silver) and "en fisk" (a fish), but the animal is an insect. To talk about more than one, the word does not change: "to sølvfisk" (two silverfish).

en søn.explanation: "En søn" means "a son". To say son-in-law, add "sviger" (in-law) in front: "en svigersøn" (a son-in-law). To say how old a son is: "Min søn er fem år" (My son is five years old).

en søndagsmiddag.explanation: "En søndagsmiddag" means "a Sunday dinner". It is built from "en søndag" (a Sunday) and "en middag" (a dinner). The word "middag" is also in other dinners, such as "en julemiddag" (a Christmas dinner).

en søster.explanation: "En søster" means "a sister". To say a sister shares only one parent, use "en halvsøster" (a half sister): "Min halvsøster bor i Aarhus" (My half sister lives in Aarhus). The plural is "søstre", not "søstere": "Jeg har to søstre" (I have two sisters).
